thread.title_full: Maricopa County Election Workers Cleared After Late-Night Tabulation Center Video Referred to FBI

author: FOX10Phoenix
title: Maricopa County Election Workers Cleared After Late-Night Tabulation Center Video Referred to FBI
text:
Maricopa County election workers were cleared after a late-night tabulation center video was referred to the FBI and County Attorney, who closed the cases with no wrongdoing found.
Maricopa County election workers were cleared of wrongdoing after a video showing them inside the tabulation center late at night on Oct. 7 was referred to the FBI and the County Attorney, officials said. Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap forwarded the video, submitted by a citizen, to law enforcement before it circulated on social media.
The Maricopa County Board of Supervisors said the employees were performing authorized software updates and election data uploads. Supervisor Kate Brophy McGee, chairwoman of the board, said the FBI and County Attorney have closed the cases with no wrongdoing found.
Investigation Finds No Wrongdoing
The video and photos showed workers inside the secured facility late at night on Oct. 7. They sparked questions and speculation on social media about what employees were doing there.
Brophy McGee stated plainly that there was no incident and that it was simply people working late at night. In a joint statement, Brophy McGee and Vice-Chair Debbie Lesko said the workers were setting up software used in the ballot duplication process on computers isolated from the internet.
Heap said his office received the video from a citizen and forwarded it to law enforcement before it circulated on social media. He explained that if questionable things are seen happening in a secured facility after it has been locked down and after Logic and Accuracy testing, it is appropriate to hand those over.
Heap added that his office did what it was required to do. He denied alleging wrongdoing but criticized county leaders for taking too long to explain the activity publicly.
County Officials Push Back on Referral
Brophy McGee said the room is livestreamed 24 hours a day and argued Heap should have contacted county officials before referring the video to law enforcement. She expressed frustration over the doxxing of election workers.
She said county officials should have been called directly to ask what their people were doing, rather than sending it straight to the FBI. Heap responded that waiting too long to put out facts undermines public confidence that they are being told the whole truth.
He said he would have liked to see the county do a better job of informing the public up front when issues arise. The disagreement highlights tensions over how election security concerns are handled and communicated in Maricopa County.
Social Media Speculation and Public Trust
Photos circulating on social media raised questions about elections staff working late at night at the Maricopa County tabulation center. The county's response came after the video had already spread online.
The incident underscores the challenges election officials face in balancing transparency with the need to protect workers from harassment. Both the FBI and the County Attorney have closed their cases, finding no wrongdoing by the employees involved.
Brophy McGee noted that the workers were doxxed as a result of the speculation. The county emphasized that the activity was routine and part of authorized election preparation.
Heap maintained that forwarding the video was the appropriate step under the circumstances. The board maintained that a simple phone call could have resolved the matter before it became public.
